issues.quote: The low notes are the hours. Each quarter is a doubled note. After the quarter come the high notes, one for each minute past it.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says nothing about how the repeater sounds or how time can be read from its strikes.
issues.misreading: A solver could treat the strike pattern as a way to fix the exact time of the chime, adding a clock-reading method the sheet does not give.

issues.quote: He meant it to strike the first minute of the new century.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no target time for the repeater and no date beyond the clock readings.
issues.misreading: A solver could read this as a specific moment the repeater was set to sound, such as midnight, which is a time not supported by any fact.

issues.quote: I regulated my own watch myself, Inspector. I do not let anyone else's hand near it.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says only that her watch was exact at the nine o'clock inspection. It says nothing about how or by whom it was regulated.
issues.misreading: A solver could infer that her watch is especially reliable or was under her sole control, which goes beyond the single reading the sheet gives.
